disclaimer: This is general guidance only and is not a substitute for advice from a qualified agricultural extension officer. Conditions and best practices may vary by region and guava variety.
description: No disease has been detected on this leaf. The tree appears healthy. Maintaining tree health through consistent good agricultural practices is the most effective way to prevent diseases from establishing.
immediate_actions: Continue routine care — watering, nutrition, and canopy management.
Take this opportunity to inspect neighbouring trees as a routine precaution.
spread_prevention: Maintain good orchard hygiene — remove fallen fruit, leaves, and dead wood regularly.
Avoid introducing untested planting material from outside the grove.
Disinfect pruning tools between trees as a standard habit, even when no disease is visible.
Ensure adequate spacing and pruning to keep the canopy open and well-ventilated.
Avoid waterlogging around tree roots — ensure good drainage in the planting area.
long_term_monitoring: Inspect leaves, fruit, and stems at least once a month and after any heavy rain or extreme weather.
Watch for early warning signs such as unusual spots, discolouration, wilting, or distorted growth.
Consult a local agricultural extension officer periodically for seasonal guidance and regional disease alerts.
Keep records of the tree's appearance over time so changes are easier to identify early.
